title: Code inventory
description: What already exists where a stated change will land: the modules involved, the conventions the area follows, what must not be rebuilt, and what the change risks breaking. The code-side counterpart of impact-analysis, which maps a domain model against stored knowledge — same shape, different subject. Every convention carries a path and every risk carries its consumers, because an assertion without one is something the producer assumed rather than found. Nothing here says how to make the change: a survey that recommended a design would have made the planning decision while calling it an observation.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

survey_id.description: Stable identifier for this survey, supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

producer.description: What performed the survey. Not a const: the contract requires the artifact, not a particular producer of it.

change.description: The change as the caller stated it, carried forward verbatim. A survey read without the intention it was made against cannot be judged for scope.

modules.description: One entry per module, sorted by path. Empty is the greenfield case and a real answer.

does.description: What the module does, in one sentence, in terms of behavior rather than of the files it contains.

relation.description: `touched` the change must modify it; `depends_on` the change calls it unchanged; `adjacent` neither, but a planner needs to know it is there.

reason.description: What makes it that relation. Restating the relation is not a reason.

conventions.description: Patterns the area already follows. Where the area is internally inconsistent, both forms appear and the note says which is more recent — a planner choosing between them needs to know one is drift rather than a rule.

seen_at.description: A path where the convention can be observed. Required: a convention asserted without one is a convention the producer assumed.

note.description: Where the repository states a rule the code diverges from, or where a second inconsistent form exists.

must_not_duplicate.description: What already exists that the change would otherwise rebuild. The section that pays for the survey.

provides.description: What it already does, and why the change would otherwise write it again.

risks.description: What could break. A risk with no named consumer is a worry rather than a finding, which is why consumers is required.

consumers.description: The callers or dependents that would notice, by path.

evidence.description: What in the code makes the producer say so.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs that no other field holds — most importantly, where the area found is larger or smaller than the stated change implies. Trimming the survey to fit the intention would hide exactly that.
